content.text:
I've got enough of the picture. Before I write code, here's what's already in place, a proposed design, and two decisions that change what I build.

## What's already there

- **Scene Bench** builds image, sound and motion briefs locally and only lets you copy them (`scene-bench.tsx:560`). Judgement and narration both already use a `SceneProviderCapability` (`{ available, destination, costLabel }`), so generation can plug into the same pattern.
- **Bring-your-own models**: `AiSettings.perFeature` with `resolveFeatureConfig` already routes each feature to a writer-chosen provider and model. Providers already store models.dev `modelModalities`, so I can list the models whose `output` includes `"image"` without hard-coding any.
- **AI SDK 6** ships a stable `generateImage`. One code path covers OpenAI, Google, and any OpenAI-compatible `/images/generations` endpoint. That last one is how "add your own model" works for Together, a local ComfyUI wrapper, and similar.
- **Gap:** nothing on the server actually meters the $10/month Pro credit. Hosted voice is protected only by the Pro check and a rate limit. If we spend Twyne's own key on images, a real monthly cap has to come first. Without it, one writer can run up an unbounded bill.

## Proposed design

**1. Generation as a reader's-mind mirror, not illustration.** The useful thing an image model does here is fill gaps. Every detail it invents is a detail the passage left to the reader. So instead of "make a pretty picture":
- **Literal reading:** the prompt says to render only what the excerpt states and keep everything else neutral. Empty, flat areas show where description is missing.
- **Imagined reading:** the model fills gaps freely, the way a reader would.
- **Afterward, a cheap text-model pass compares the image with the inventory.** It lists what came from the source, what was invented (where you were silent), and anything that contradicts the source. Those invented details become one-click proposals in the existing ideas list, under dimensions like light and sound.

**2. Opt-in at two levels.** Generation is off until you turn it on in Settings, under a new `scene-image` feature. Then every run needs an explicit "Generate (destination · cost)" click. Nothing runs automatically or on a keystroke.

**3. Your own models.** Pick any provider or model with image output, or enter an OpenAI-compatible base URL and model ID. Usage goes to the local ledger as BYOK.

**4. Results stay on the device**, keyed to the passage snapshot in IndexedDB like proposals are. An "Insert into manuscript" action reuses the existing upload flow.

**5. Images only for now.** Sound and motion keep their copyable briefs. Video generation costs dollars per clip and no provider shares one API for it, so I'd add those later behind the same opt-in.

options.label: Full loop (Recommended)
options.description: Literal/imagined modes, generation, then the comparison pass that sorts details into from-source, invented and contradicted, with one-click proposals.

options.label: Generate only
options.description: Literal/imagined modes and generation with an on-device gallery. Comparison comes later.

content.text:
Scene Bench is now connected to real image generation, and I doubled the hosted per-picture budget as you asked. Nothing is committed. App typecheck is clean, and the 32 targeted tests plus 37 feature-routing and usage tests pass. **Not yet tested:** I haven't run a real generation, either through Twyne's hosted model or a BYOK key, and I haven't opened it in the browser.

**How it works**
- **Off by default.** It stays off until you turn it on in Settings under the new **Scene Pictures** section. Even then, nothing runs until you press **Generate picture** in the bench.
- **Two ways to picture a passage:**
  - **Only what's written:** the model is told to draw only what the passage states and leave everything else plain grey, so the gaps are visible.
  - **As a reader fills it in:** the model fills the gaps freely, and your saved ideas go into the prompt.
- **Comparison pass.** A vision model then sorts each detail in the picture into one of three groups:
  - **Contradicts the page:** what a reader might get wrong.
  - **Left to the reader:** what the page doesn't say.
  - **Taken from the page:** details your words already supply, with the quoted passage text. If the model quotes something that isn't actually in the passage, it gets moved to "left to the reader".
- **Keep as an idea.** Any contradicted or invented detail can be added to your existing ideas list with one click. The manuscript stays unchanged.
- Pictures are saved on the device for that exact selection and mode, and can be downloaded. Copyable briefs are still there for sound, motion, or other tools.

**Paying for it**
- **Hosted:** uses the Not Organic gateway's `image` alias (`convex/sceneMedia.ts`). There's no monthly picture cap; the only limits are your wallet balance and a 6-per-minute guard against runaway loops. Each picture carries a **$0.50** cost ceiling (`SCENE_PICTURE_BUDGET_MICROS`), plus $0.05 for the comparison. The bench always shows the short warning that pictures use credit quickly, and adds a separate low-balance warning with an "Add credit" link below $1.
- **Your own models:** OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible image endpoint. Settings' model routing has two new entries: **Scene Pictures** (lists models.dev models that output images) and **Scene Picture Comparison** (lists vision models). You can still type any model ID by hand. Usage goes into your local usage log.

**Before this works in production**
- The new Convex module needs deploying.
- I confirmed the gateway serves `/v1/images/generations`. I couldn't confirm that Twyne's issued tokens get the `infer:image` scope, or which upstream model and price sit behind the `image` alias. If a picture usually costs more than $0.50, the gateway will refuse it rather than charge more, so check that ceiling against the real price.
- The general low-credit warning only appears in Scene Bench for now. `lowCreditWarning()` in `src/utils/scene-media-credit.ts` is ready to reuse elsewhere, for example on the pricing page.

The working tree also has changes I didn't make: Typst, the editor, `global.css`, the pricing page, and some new editorial-roles files. I left all of those alone.
